info.title: FCP admin API
info.description: The Ferrous Communications Platform admin API. Every request carries `Authorization: Bearer <token>`: the static token, a session's access token from `/auth/login` (refreshed by `/auth/refresh` with its HttpOnly cookie), or an API token (`docs/API_TOKENS.md`). Errors are `{error, code, details}`, times are RFC 3339, and lists are `{data, next_cursor, total}` paged by `limit` and `cursor`.

put.description:
PUT /api/v1/users/:username/digest-password

This sets a separate password for SIP authentication, providing security isolation
between API/web access and SIP phone registration (Cisco CUCM style).

**Security Benefits:**
- Compromised SIP credentials don't expose API/admin access
- Different password policies for phones vs admin users
- Separate rotation schedules for SIP and API credentials

**Note:** If digest_password is not set (NULL), the main password is used for SIP.

newest first.

post.summary:
POST /api/v1/devices/:id/render — the device's configuration as its
phone would get it now (credentials included), from its template or
the one given.

POST /api/v1/firmware — upload an image (multipart: `vendor`,
`version`, `models` (comma-separated patterns), `notes`, and `file`,
whose name is the one it is served under). The platform
administrator's.

delete.summary:
DELETE /api/v1/firmware/:id — remove an image no tenant targets. The
platform administrator's.

get.summary:
GET /api/v1/firmware/targets — the tenant's targets, each with how many
of its phones run its version.

post.summary: POST /api/v1/firmware/targets

put.summary:
PUT /api/v1/firmware/targets/:id — change a target: another image, the
pilot set, or `all` to roll it out.

delete.summary:
DELETE /api/v1/firmware/targets/:id — phones keep what they run; their
templates stop naming an image.
DELETE /api/v1/branding — no brand: the apps show their own.

post.summary:
POST /api/v1/branding/assets — upload a file as the body: a PNG, JPEG,
WebP or SVG image, or Ogg, MP3 or WAV audio, at most 5 MB. What it is
comes from its bytes. The same file again is the same asset.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The file's name, for the admin's page.

delete.summary:
DELETE /api/v1/branding/assets/{sha256} — one the brand names is
refused (409).

get.summary:
GET /api/v1/branding/deployment-profile — the tenant's softphone profile
(Anvil's `docs/MANAGED_INSTALLS.md` §2.1): this admin's address as the
server, the tenant's first login domain, its sign-in, and its brand with
the files, for `Anvil-…-setup.exe /PROFILE=` or Windows policy.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description:
`zip` (the default): `profile.json` and the brand's files; `json`:
`profile.json` alone; `reg`: the same settings as Windows policy.

parameters.name: sign_in
parameters.description:
`auto`, `sso` or `password`; unset, `sso` when the tenant allows no
password, else `auto`.

parameters.name: lock_server
parameters.description: Whether the server field is locked; unset, it is.

parameters.name: username_from_system
parameters.description:
Fill the username in from Windows' user principal name; unset, when
the tenant has a login domain.

200.description: The profile: a .zip, its profile.json (format=json) or a .reg (format=reg)

get.summary:
GET /api/v1/provisioning/redirection — each service and the tenant's
account with it.

delete.summary:
DELETE /api/v1/provisioning/redirection/:service — forget the account;
phones registered with it stay registered at the vendor.

post.summary:
POST /api/v1/provisioning/redirection/:service/check — ask the service
whether the account's credentials work.

POST /api/v1/provisioning/redirection/:service/sync — register every
phone of the service's vendor not yet registered (an account made after
its devices).

POST /api/v1/devices/:id/redirection — register the device's phone
with its vendor's service now (again, if it was).

POST /api/v1/devices/:id/resync — tell the phone to fetch its
configuration again, with its vendor's NOTIFY (`docs/PROVISIONING.md`
§8), sent by a call manager to each contact it is registered from.

POST /api/v1/devices/:id/push-test — send the device's apps a test push
(`docs/PUSH.md` §2.3) through a call manager with the publisher's keys:
the app shows it and ends it at once. Whether each was taken.

POST /api/v1/config-templates/:id/resync — tell every phone this
template is rendered for to fetch its configuration again
(`docs/PROVISIONING.md` §8).

POST /api/v1/devices/import — phones by MAC, each checked before any is
made: all are made, or none and every row's fault is named.

get.summary:
GET /api/v1/provisioning/pending — phones waiting to be claimed, the
most recently seen first.

post.summary:
POST /api/v1/provisioning/pending/:mac/claim — make the pending phone a
device in one step: its vendor and model as it gave them, an owner, a
template if one is named.

201.description: The device, with its provisioning token shown once

delete.summary:
DELETE /api/v1/provisioning/pending/:mac — forget a pending phone; it
comes back if it fetches again.

ApiTokenResponse.description: Response model for an API token (never includes a hash).

scope.description:
`admin` (the admin API under its permissions) or `personal` (its
maker's own `/me` routes).

created_by.description:
The maker's username; empty for a token made with the static token or
before makers were recorded.

legacy_full_access.description:
A token made before permissions were checked, carrying `admin` or
`*`: it reaches everything in its tenant. Review and replace it.

previous_secret_valid_until.description: Until when the secret a rotation replaced still opens the token.

AppClientRequest.description: The app, as it names itself.

client_name.description: What the app calls itself on this machine ("Alice's MacBook").

install_id.description: Kept by the install across sign-ins.

AppDeviceResponse.description:
The install's device and its SIP account: the password is shown here
once, at each sign-in, and never again.

realm.description: The realm the password is hashed in, as the registrars challenge.

AppTokenRequest.description:
What `POST /auth/app/token` takes, as JSON or a form (RFC 6749 §4.1.3,
§6).

client_name.description: With `authorization_code`: the app, as `/auth/app/sessions` takes it.

refresh_token.description: Opaque; rotated on every refresh, so keep the newest.

refresh_expires_in.description: Seconds the session lasts unless refreshed.

session_id.description: The session, as `/me/sessions` and the audit log name it.

oneOf.description: The install's device, at a sign-in; absent from a refresh.

request.description: The `app` the sign-in page was opened with.

redirect_url.description: The app's loopback address with `code` and `state`.

file.description:
The picture: PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP. The field may also be named
`avatar`.

available.description: Funds that may still be spent (balance + credit limit).

oneOf.description: The tenant's prepaid/credit balance, when one is configured.

sha256.description: Hex SHA-256: what the brand names it by.

mime.description: What the file is, from its bytes.

url.description: Where apps fetch it, without credentials.

BrandColors.description:
The colors of one theme, each `#RRGGBB` or `#RRGGBBAA`; one unset is
the app's own.

BrandDialPlan.description:
Hints for the app's dialer: prefixes it takes off what is dialed, and
short codes it turns into addresses.

BrandRequest.description: The tenant's brand, as its administrator writes it: assets by hash.

app_name.description: The app's name, as the tenant's people see it.

oneOf.description: The dark theme's; unset, the app derives its own.

icon.description: An uploaded PNG, JPEG or WebP image's hash.

ringtones.description: Uploaded audio, by hash; at most one the default.

BrandResponse.description: The tenant's brand, with what its assets are.

brand_url.description: Where the tenant's softphones fetch it.

BrandRingtone.description: A ringtone the app offers, by its asset's hash.

CallControlResponse.description: What the node answered a control with.

party.description: Who was held, transferred or redirected.

playback_id.description: A playback, for play and say.

CallerIdPolicy.description: How a user's caller ID leaves on a trunk.

CallingResponse.description:
The settings as the API shows them: targets in their string form
(`voicemail`, `number:+15551234567`, `ext:2001`, `user:<id>`, a SIP URI).

hold_music.description: A prompt's id, `none` for silence, or absent for the tenant's music.

after_hours_schedule_id.description: The user's hours and where calls go outside them (§3.5).

oneOf.description:
Find-me / follow-me (§3.6): `enabled`, and `steps` of `targets`
(`devices`, `ext:…`, `number:+…`, `user:…`, a SIP URI), `ring_secs`
and `confirm`.

class_of_service_id.description: The user's class of service (§3.7); `None` is the tenant's default.

oneOf.description:
The user as an executive (§3.10): `enabled`, `filter` (`all`,
`external`, `none`), `alert` (`assistants`,
`assistants_and_executive`), and `assistants` (`user_id`,
`opted_in`) in order.

kind.description: What the record is a record of: `call`, `queue`, `conference`, `gateway`.

direction.description:
`inbound`, `outbound` or `internal` once the pipeline has enriched
the record; absent until then.

trunk_id.description:
Which trunk carried the call (`docs/TENANT_TRUNKS.md` §4): two
tenants may both have a "carrier-a".

recording_consent.description:
`announced`, `failed`, `not_required` or `refused` when the call was
to be recorded; absent otherwise.

CivicElements.description:
The RFC 5139 civic address elements beyond city, state, postal code and
country, which [`E911Address`] carries as fields of its own.

house_number.description: `HNO`: the numeric part of the house number (`1455`).

name.description: `NAM`: the name of the place (`Example HQ`).

ClaimDeviceRequest.description: What a claimed or imported phone becomes.

name.description: Unset: its vendor, model and MAC.

owner_user_id.description: Its owner, by id or by username.

config_template_id.description: Unset: picked by vendor and model when the phone fetches.

ClaimMapping.description: Which claims become the user's names.

username.description:
The username of a user made just in time; the part before the `@`
when the claim is an address. Falls back to the email's.

groups.description:
A list of strings: the user's groups (Entra ID sends ids, Okta
and Google Workspace names, when asked to).

ClassOfServiceRequest.description:
What a class is written as. `allowed` unset allows everything;
`max_calls` unset is two, `null` no limit.

ClassReport.description: What one class of data gave up to an export.

files.description: Media files put in the bundle.

missing_files.description:
Media files that are the subject's but could not be read from this
host, with why.

held.description: Items under a legal hold (exported like the rest).

ClusterNodeInfo.description: Information about a single cluster node, enriched with derived fields.

started_at.description:
When the node started, as RFC 3339 in the admin API
(`docs/DEVELOPER_SURFACE.md` §3, phase 2b); epoch seconds here.

region.description: Deployment region the node advertises, when it has one.

video_budget.description: Video budget per device, when the node advertises one.

oneOf.description:
What the node will carry and what it is carrying, when it keeps
limits (`docs/CAPACITY_AND_SURVIVABILITY.md` §7).

calls_left.description: Calls this node will still take, when it says what it allows.

oneOf.description:
The node's own view of the cluster, when it does not look whole
(`docs/MULTI_REGION_FOLLOWUPS.md` §2.3).

ClusterNodeStatus.description: Status of a cluster node, derived from its Redis key TTL.

ClusterSitesResponse.description:
Response for GET /api/v1/cluster/sites: every tenant's sites, as the
tenant API shows one.

ClusterStats.description: Aggregate statistics across all cluster nodes.

nodes_by_region.description: Nodes per advertised region; nodes without one are not counted here.

nodes_with_partial_view.description:
Nodes whose own view of the cluster does not look whole — most
often every node of a region that has lost the others (§2.3).

version_skew.description:
More than one release is running: an upgrade under way, or one
that stopped half way.

ClusterView.description:
This node's view, as `/status`, the heartbeat record and the
`system.cluster_view_changed` event carry it.

since.description: When the current state began (Unix seconds); absent while whole.

lost_regions.description: The regions whose every node went at once.

view_age_secs.description:
Seconds since discovery last worked — how old the member list is.
Absent before the first discovery.

database_reachable.description:
Whether the node reaches its database, when it has a probe and the
view is not whole.

value.description: A configuration section: a JSON object.

listen.description: A `call` contact may listen in to the emergency call.

ContactInput.description:
A contact on the way in: either the plain string the API took before
block 2, read by its shape, or a typed object.

ContactReadiness.description:
One contact and how it has fared (§8.4): a tenant should be able to
see that its notifications work before it needs them to.

site.description: The site whose contact this is; absent for the tenant's own.

listen.description: Whether this contact may listen in to the call.

issues.description: What keeps this contact from being delivered to.

last_delivery_at.description: When anything was last delivered to it.

last_test_at.description: When a `933` test call's notice last reached it.

ContactResponse.description: One notification contact as the API shows it.

listen.description:
A `call` contact who may listen in to the emergency call once told
(`docs/E911.md` "Listening in").

issues.description: What keeps this contact from being delivered to, empty when it can.

CreateApiTokenRequest.description: Request body for creating a new admin API token.

permissions.description:
Permission names (`Permission::as_str`), or `admin` for everything
the maker may grant.

CreateApiTokenResponse.description: Response body after creating a token (includes the one-time secret).

sip_username.description: Credentials of the device's own (§3.8): both, or neither.

hoteling_host.description: A shared phone users may log in on.

vendor.description:
The phone's vendor (`docs/PROVISIONING.md` §5); unset, read from
the MAC where its prefix is a vendor's.

line_keys.description: The keys programmed on the phone.

provisioning_token.description:
Optional per-device provisioning token. If omitted for a device with a
MAC address, a token is generated and returned once in the create response.

schedule_id.description: A schedule of the tenant; empty clears it.

closed_target.description:
A call target (`voicemail`, `number:+…`, `ext:…`, `flow:…`,
`queue:…`, a SIP URI); empty clears it.

shared.description: A shared line: its devices share its appearances (§3.9).

max_appearances.description: How many calls a shared line carries at once (1 to 24).

barge_in.description: A phone on the shared line may barge into an active appearance.

hold_music.description:
The number's hold music: a prompt of the tenant, `none` for
silence, or empty for the tenant's.

emergency_contacts.description: The site's emergency contacts, as `/emergency/config` takes them.

notify_tenant_contacts.description: Whether the tenant's contacts are told too (true when unsaid).

flow_id.description:
A flow of the tenant's to handle a call this mailbox would take —
say something, ring someone, a queue, or a message after all. Unset:
the mailbox takes it.

cidr.description: A range (`10.1.2.0/24`) or a single address.

location_id.description: The site an address on this network is at.

CreatePersonalTokenRequest.description: Request body for creating a personal API token.

site_id.description: The site whose phones answer this number; empty to answer it here.

schedule_id.description: A schedule of the tenant; empty clears it.

closed_target.description: A call target; empty clears it.

agent_group_id.description: A group of the tenant whose members are agents too; empty clears it.

CreateTenantRequest.description: Request to create a new tenant

sip_domains.description: SIP domains to claim on behalf of the new tenant.

platform_trunk_fallback.description:
Whether the platform's trunks may carry this tenant's calls when it
has none of its own that can (`docs/TENANT_TRUNKS.md` §5). True
unless said otherwise.

oneOf.description: How the tenant dials and keeps time.

login_domains.description: Email domains whose people are this tenant's.

oneOf.description: How the tenant's people may sign in.

Currency used when this entry creates the tenant's balance row.

external_ref.description:
Reference to the external billing system's record (invoice id,
payment id, ...).

site_id.description: The site this trunk runs at; empty to make it the cloud's own.

Send numbers in E.164 (`+15183217034`), as the tenant's country
reads what was dialled, before the digit plan: what Twilio needs.

The web password. Left out, the user has none and signs in only
through the tenant's identity provider (`docs/IDENTITY_AND_DEVICES.md`
phase 2); their SIP password is then generated.

Optional SIP password retained for device auto-provisioning templates.

When set, this becomes the user's SIP digest password and is exposed by
provisioning as `${sip_password}` for vendors that cannot use HA1.

CreateWebhookRequest.description: What a webhook is made with.

DataClass.description: The classes of data a hold can cover.

reached.description: Whether this host reached the dead letters.

allOf.description: RFC 5139 civic elements, as `/v1/locations` takes them.

DeclaredLocationResponse.description: A user's declared location: where they are when no network places them.

current.description: False once it has expired: the platform stops using it.

DestinationClass.description: What kind of destination a dialled number is.

A tenant's own word on a range of numbers: `prefix` is E.164 when it
starts with `+` (`+1900`), or the digits as dialled otherwise (`118`).

DeviceAppResponse.description: An app install's session, on its device.

signed_in.description: Whether the app is signed in now.

signed_in_at.description: When it signed in, while it is.

last_seen.description: When it last refreshed its session, while it is signed in.

DeviceFetchResponse.description: One fetch of a device's file.

DeviceRedirectionResponse.description: Where a device stands with its vendor's service.

with_credentials.description: Whether the phone was given its own credentials through the service.

vendor.description:
`yealink`, `polycom`, `grandstream`, `cisco`, `fanvil` or `snom`:
with the model, it picks the template when the device names none.

firmware_target_version.description:
The version its tenant's firmware target points it at
(`docs/PROVISIONING.md` §11), and whether it runs it: `current`,
`behind`, `unknown` (it has not said). Unset without a target.

sip_username.description:
The username of the device's own credentials; the password and its
hash are never returned (`docs/ENTERPRISE_CALLING.md` §3.8).

hoteling_host.description: A shared phone users may log in on.

push_provider.description:
The provider that wakes it when it sleeps (`apns`, `fcm`), while it
is registered with a push address (`docs/PUSH.md` §2.1).

line_keys.description: The keys programmed on the phone, in order.

e911_trust_location.description:
Whether this device is trusted to send its own location with a
call (`docs/E911_BLOCK_2.md` §6.3); `null` follows its type.

DirectoryEntry.description: Someone, or something, in the tenant's directory.

kind.description:
`user`, or `extension` for one that rings no user (a queue, a
flow, a number).

user_id.description: The user's id; unset for an extension.

presence.description:
Where they are: `open`, `closed`, `away`, `busy`, `on_the_phone`
or `ringing`; unset when nothing is known.

DiscoverRequest.description: What a login may sign in with.

login.description: A username, or an email address.

DiscoverResponse.description: Where a login signs in, and how.

tenant_id.description: The tenant the login's email domain belongs to, when it is one.

methods.description:
The ways in: `password`, and `sso` when the tenant has identity
providers to sign in with.

providers.description:
The tenant's identity providers: a button each on the login page,
which goes to `/api/v1/auth/sso/{id}/start`.

DiscoveredProvider.description: An identity provider a login can sign in through.

allOf.description:
RFC 5139 civic elements (`house_number`, `street_name`,
`street_suffix`, `unit`, …), beside the lines above
(`docs/E911_BLOCK_2.md` §5.1).

validated.description:
Whether a validator has confirmed this address. Read-only: an
address is validated by `POST …/e911/validate`, never by claiming
it here (`docs/E911_BLOCK_2.md` §7).

validated_by.description: The validator that confirmed it, and the reference it gave.

trunk_id.description: Which trunk carried it; a name is unique only within its tenant.

sip_status.description: The final SIP status, once the call has ended.

duration_secs.description: Seconds from answer to end, for an answered call.

delivery.description: How the location travelled: `elin`, `pidf_lo`, `elin+pidf_lo`, or none.

location_structured.description: Whether the location's street went out in civic elements.

geolocation_error.description: The `Geolocation-Error` a trunk answered the location with.

test_call_mode.description:
Who answers a test call: `local`, this platform reading back what a
live call would carry, or `carrier`, the carrier's test service.

contacts.description:
Who is told when an emergency call is placed, typed by channel
(`docs/E911_BLOCK_2.md` §8.1).

notify_contacts.description:
The same contacts as the plain strings this field has always
carried, for clients written before block 2.

trust_device_locations.description:
Device types whose own location (a PIDF-LO they send with the call)
this tenant trusts.

declared_location_ttl_secs.description: How long a user's declared location stands, in seconds.

configured.description: False when the tenant has never saved a config (defaults shown).

EncryptionStatus.description: Snapshot of a backend's encryption state.

enabled.description: Whether secret columns are sealed on write.

kek_id.description: Identifier of the key-encryption key wrapping the DEKs.

key_ids.description: Every DEK the backend can read with, oldest first.

items.description: Items it was (or, in a preview, would be) done to.

held.description: Items left alone because a legal hold covers them.

errors.description: Items it could not act on, with why.

ErasureReport.description: What an erasure found, did, kept and could not reach.

held_by.description: The holds that kept items, by id, with their matters.

not_reached.description: What the erasure cannot reach, and when it goes.

tables.description: A tenant's deletion: rows removed, by table.

ErrorResponse.description:
API error response: the one shape every error under `/api/v1` has
(docs/DEVELOPER_SURFACE.md §3, phase 2), whether a handler, the auth
layer or an extractor refused the request.

error.description: The status's reason phrase, e.g. `Not Found`.

code.description:
A stable machine-readable code: the status as snake case
(`not_found`, `bad_request`, `rate_limited`, …).

ExecutiveAlert.description: Who rings for a call the filter takes.

ExecutiveFilter.description:
Which of an executive's calls their assistants take first
(`docs/ENTERPRISE_CALLING.md` §3.10).

ExecutiveRequest.description: What may change of a user as an executive.

assistants.description:
The assistants in order, each a username or a user id of the
tenant; replaces the list, keeping each one's opt-in. An admin's to
set: refused at `/me/calling`.

ExecutiveView.description:
A user as an executive, as the API shows it: user ids in their
prefixed form, as everywhere else.

ExportReport.description: What an export found, class by class, and what it could not reach.

not_exported.description:
Stores the export does not reach, with why (transit stores, operator
stores, backups).

review.description:
Recordings in which other people are heard, for the tenant to review
before handing the bundle over (`media/<class>/<id>.<ext>`).

held_by.description: The holds covering exported items, by id, with their matters.

reference.description: The tenant's own reference: a ticket, a letter.

FindMe.description:
A user's find-me: steps rung one after another once the user's own
phones have rung, before the no-answer treatment.

confirm.description:
A leg of this step that answers must press 1 before it is
connected: a mobile's voicemail does not take the call.

FindMeTarget.description: Who a find-me step rings: `devices`, or a target (`number:+…`, `ext:…`, `user:…`, a SIP URI)

FirmwareStatus.description: Where a phone stands against its target.

model_pattern.description: Unset: every model of the vendor.

oneOf.description: Unset: `pilot`.

devices.description: The tenant's phones it is for (stage aside), and where they stand.

GrantablePermission.description: A permission the caller may put on a token.

expires_at.description: Unix timestamp in seconds, or null

GroupMemberResponse.description: A member as the API answers it.

GroupRequest.description: What a group is written as.

role.description:
A role its members hold besides their own: not `super_admin`, nor

Authorization policy for presence subscriptions.

Determines which watchers are allowed to subscribe to a presentity's state.
If no policy is set for a presentity, all watchers are allowed (default open).

1. Block list (AOR exact match) → deny
2. Per-event block list → deny
3. Block patterns (domain wildcard) → deny
4. Allow list (AOR exact match) → allow

6. Allow patterns (domain wildcard) → allow
7. Time window check → deny if outside windows

VideoDeviceBudget.description:
One device's video budget on a node, in work units: one unit is a
thousandth of one execution unit's time per second (on the host, a
millicore of one codec-pool thread). `left` is what a new room or
participant may still cost here.

codecs.description: SDP names of the codecs the device *encodes* (`H264`, `VP8`, …).

left.description:
What a new room or participant may still cost here: on a device
with engines, the tightest engine's.

oneOf.description:
A GPU's engines, each a budget of its own (FCP §15.8): NVENC,
NVDEC and the compute cores saturate separately, and placement
wants the encoder's. Absent on the host, and on a node from
before engines were advertised.

VideoEngines.description: The three budgets of a GPU.

ViewState.description: What this node's view of the cluster looks like.

WebhookDeliveryOutcome.description: What one delivery attempt came to.

response_body.description: The start of what the receiver answered.

next_retry_at.description: When the dispatcher tries again; none once delivered or given up.

WebhookEvent.description: The body of every delivery (the spec's `webhooks` section).

event_id.description: Unique per delivery: a receiver may drop one it has seen.

WebhookEventType.description: An event type a webhook may subscribe to.

category.description: `call`: subscribe to all of them with `call.*`.

events.description:
Event types delivered: names from `/webhooks/event-types`, a
category's `call.*`, or `*`. Empty is every event.

secret_prefix.description: The first characters of the secret, to tell secrets apart.

previous_secret_valid_until.description: Until when the secret a rotation replaced also signs deliveries.

WebhookWithSecret.description:
A webhook just made or rotated, with its secret: the only time the
secret is shown.

WeeklyWindow.description:
A span of hours on some days: `start` to `end` local time; an `end`
before its `start` runs past midnight into the next day, and an `end`
equal to its `start` is the whole day.

client_address.description: The address the caller was seen at, when one placed them.

declared_age_secs.description: For a declared location, how long ago the user declared it.

me.MailboxResponse.description: Mailbox response (reuse same shape as admin).

media.RecordingResponse.description: What the node answered a recording request with.

recording_id.description: The recording's id, when one started.

path.description: The file it is written to, when one started.

consent.description: What the parties were told: `announced`, `failed` or `not_required`.

bearer.description: The static token, a session JWT, or an `fcp_…` API token
